title: Opening a text block, and when it is a constant

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to `String s = """content""";`, with the content on the same line as the opening delimiter?

options.text: It compiles to the string content
options.says: The page shows this exact line as a compilation error: the opening delimiter must be followed by a line terminator.

options.text: It is refused by the compiler
options.says: The page says no content may sit on the opening delimiter's line; the content has to start on the next line.

options.text: It compiles to content plus a newline
options.says: The page gives no value to this line; it marks it as a compilation error, since content must start on the line after the opening delimiter.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

questions.stem: Per this page, which of these can be a `case` label in a `switch` on a `String`?

options.text: A static final field set to a text block plus a literal with +
options.says: The page says text blocks joined only with other constants stay compile-time constants, and a case label needs one.

options.text: A static final field set to a text block with .formatted("World")
options.says: The page says calling formatted() computes the value at run time, so the result is not a compile-time constant.

options.text: A static final field set to a text block plus a parameter with +
options.says: The page says a text block joined with a non-constant expression is not a compile-time constant.
